research_rationale:
Executive Order 11298 of August 14, 1966 (31 FR 10915), Prescribing the Interest Rate for Deposit of Savings of Members of the Uniformed Services, is a single paragraph. Acting under section 1035 of title 10, United States Code, as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, it prescribes that amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services under that section accrue interest at ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, and states that the order is effective September 1, 1966. The held Federal Register page text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11298.txt, GPO Federal Register of August 17, 1966) carries the heading directly above the paragraph, and the order has no other paragraph. The September 1, 1966 sentence is a start date, not an end. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 11298 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11298.txt). The OFR executive-order catalog records no disposition note for the order, and the three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog; coverage notes read) report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (Office of the Law Revision Counsel, edition current through 2026-10-09; changes enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1035 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1035(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1035.txt) provides that interest at a rate prescribed by the President, not to exceed 10 percent a year, accrues on amounts deposited under that section, so the statute the order implements remains in force and the prescribed rate equals its ceiling. The same held section text still provides special treatment for members in a missing status during the Vietnam conflict, the Persian Gulf conflict or a contingency operation, and its amendment notes record a 1991 amendment (Pub. L. 102-190, section 639(a)), so the deposit program was still being legislated after 1973. The 1989 codification prints an editorial note that on January 26, 1973 a terminal date of March 28, 1973 was prescribed by DOD Instruction 1348.15; the earlier-end check below tests that note and explains why it does not end the order. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.

AWARDS TO THE MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES
By virtue of the authority vested in,me by section 1124 (b) and (e) 
o f title 10, United States Code, and section 301 of title 3, United States 
Code, and as President of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Any suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement by 
a member of the armed forces that contributes to the efficiency, econ­
omy, or other improvement of operations of the Government of the 
United States through its adoption or use by an executive department 
or agency other than the executive department having jurisdiction 
over the armed force of the member concerned may be the basis for 
honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transporta­
tion in the case of a member of the Coast Guard when it is not operat­
ing as a service in the Navy or by the Secretary of Defense in the case 
of any other member of the .armed forces.
S ec . | |  An executive department or agency that adopts or uses the 
suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement o f a member of the 
armed forces who is not under its jurisdiction may recommend to the 
Department of Defense or to the Department of Transportation, as 
appropriate, a cash award or honorary recognition o f the member 
and shall justify its recommendation with appropriate documentation 
and explanation o f how the suggestion, invention, or scientific achieve­
ment contributes to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement of 
the operations of the Government of the United States. Awards shall 
be made under regulations to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation, as appropriate. The regulations 
of the Department o f Defense and Department o f Transportation 
may include designations of officials to whom authority for receiving, 
evaluating, and making awards may .  be assigned.
Sec. -3 .. No cash awards hereunder for a single suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement may exceed $25,000 regardless of the number 
o f agencies or departments which may adopt or use the suggestion, 
invention, or scientific achievement.
S ec. 4. Funds to cover the costs o f cash awards to members of the 
armed forces shall be transferred from the account o f any executive 
department or agency which recommends the award to the appropriate 
account o f the Department o f Transportation or the Department of 
Defense, as the case may be. When several executive departments or 
agencies benefit from the adoption or use o f the suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement, the amount transferred from each such 
benefiting department or agency to the Department of Transportation 
or the Department of Defense to cover the proportionate share o f the 
cost of the cash award shall be determined under procedures prescribed 
by the Civil Service Commission in accordance with the same guide­
lines and standards applying to awards to civilian employees.

By virtue of the authority vested in,me by section 1124 (b) and (e) 
o f title 10, United States Code, and section 301 of title 3, United States

S ection  1. Any suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement by

over the armed force of the member concerned may be the basis for 
honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transporta­

ment contributes to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement of 
the operations of the Government of the United States. Awards shall 
be made under regulations to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation, as appropriate. The regulations 
of the Department o f Defense and Department o f Transportation

evaluating, and making awards may .  be assigned.

armed forces shall be transferred from the account o f any executive 
department or agency which recommends the award to the appropriate

AWARDS TO THE MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES
By virtue of the authority vested in,me by section 1124 (b) and (e) 
o f title 10, United States Code, and section 301 of title 3, United States 
Code, and as President of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Any suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement by 
a member of the armed forces that contributes to the efficiency, econ­
omy, or other improvement of operations of the Government of the 
United States through its adoption or use by an executive department 
or agency other than the executive department having jurisdiction 
over the armed force of the member concerned may be the basis for 
honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transporta­
tion in the case of a member of the Coast Guard when it is not operat­
ing as a service in the Navy or by the Secretary of Defense in the case 
of any other member of the .armed forces.
S ec . | |  An executive department or agency that adopts or uses the 
suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement o f a member of the 
armed forces who is not under its jurisdiction may recommend to the 
Department of Defense or to the Department of Transportation, as 
appropriate, a cash award or honorary recognition o f the member 
and shall justify its recommendation with appropriate documentation 
and explanation o f how the suggestion, invention, or scientific achieve­
ment contributes to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement of 
the operations of the Government of the United States. Awards shall 
be made under regulations to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation, as appropriate. The regulations 
of the Department o f Defense and Department o f Transportation 
may include designations of officials to whom authority for receiving, 
evaluating, and making awards may .  be assigned.
Sec. -3 .. No cash awards hereunder for a single suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement may exceed $25,000 regardless of the number 
o f agencies or departments which may adopt or use the suggestion, 
invention, or scientific achievement.
S ec. 4. Funds to cover the costs o f cash awards to members of the 
armed forces shall be transferred from the account o f any executive 
department or agency which recommends the award to the appropriate 
account o f the Department o f Transportation or the Department of 
Defense, as the case may be. When several executive departments or 
agencies benefit from the adoption or use o f the suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement, the amount transferred from each such 
benefiting department or agency to the Department of Transportation 
or the Department of Defense to cover the proportionate share o f the 
cost of the cash award shall be determined under procedures prescribed 
by the Civil Service Commission in accordance with the same guide­
lines and standards applying to awards to civilian employees.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11438 of December 3, 1968 (33 FR 18085), Prescribing Procedures Governing Interdepartmental Cash Awards to the Members of the Armed Forces, issued under 10 U.S.C. 1124(b) and (e) and 3 U.S.C. 301, has four numbered sections. Section 1 allows honorary recognition or a cash award for a suggestion, invention or scientific achievement of a member of the armed forces adopted by another executive department or agency, by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation. Section 2 lets the adopting agency recommend an award and requires awards under regulations of the two Secretaries. Section 3 caps a cash award at $25,000. Section 4 requires funds to be transferred from the recommending agency and procedures to be prescribed by the Civil Service Commission when several agencies benefit. The dossier's two-clause inventory ran sections 1 through 3 together, so I corrected it to four clauses with exact spans in the held Federal Register text. Later events, all amendments that leave the clauses continuing: (1) Executive Order 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055), section 2-101, lists EO 11438 among the orders in which Office of Personnel Management is substituted for Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; in EO 11438 that reference appears only in section 4. (2) Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619), section 63, strikes the Secretary of Transportation in sections 1 and 2 and the Department of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 2 and 4, inserting Homeland Security, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor; its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11438 and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so it is not a later event. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 12107 and EO 13286 section 63, as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1124 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1124 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1124.txt) still authorizes these cash awards and limits them to $25,000, and the held current 5 CFR 451.101(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-451.101.txt) states that section 4 of E.O. 11438 requires the Office of Personnel Management to prescribe procedures for covering the cost of a cash award recommended by more than one agency. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation or supersession. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.

By virtue of the authority vested in,me by section 1124 (b) and (e) 
o f title 10, United States Code, and section 301 of title 3, United States 
Code, and as President of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Any suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement by 
a member of the armed forces that contributes to the efficiency, econ­
omy, or other improvement of operations of the Government of the 
United States through its adoption or use by an executive department 
or agency other than the executive department having jurisdiction 
over the armed force of the member concerned may be the basis for 
honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transporta­
tion in the case of a member of the Coast Guard when it is not operat­
ing as a service in the Navy or by the Secretary of Defense in the case 
of any other member of the .armed forces.
S ec . | |  An executive department or agency that adopts or uses the 
suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement o f a member of the 
armed forces who is not under its jurisdiction may recommend to the 
Department of Defense or to the Department of Transportation, as 
appropriate, a cash award or honorary recognition o f the member 
and shall justify its recommendation with appropriate documentation 
and explanation o f how the suggestion, invention, or scientific achieve­
ment contributes to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement of 
the operations of the Government of the United States. Awards shall 
be made under regulations to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation, as appropriate. The regulations 
of the Department o f Defense and Department o f Transportation 
may include designations of officials to whom authority for receiving, 
evaluating, and making awards may .  be assigned.
Sec. -3 .. No cash awards hereunder for a single suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement may exceed $25,000 regardless of the number 
o f agencies or departments which may adopt or use the suggestion, 
invention, or scientific achievement.
S ec. 4. Funds to cover the costs o f cash awards to members of the 
armed forces shall be transferred from the account o f any executive 
department or agency which recommends the award to the appropriate 
account o f the Department o f Transportation or the Department of 
Defense, as the case may be. When several executive departments or 
agencies benefit from the adoption or use o f the suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement, the amount transferred from each such 
benefiting department or agency to the Department of Transportation 
or the Department of Defense to cover the proportionate share o f the 
cost of the cash award shall be determined under procedures prescribed 
by the Civil Service Commission in accordance with the same guide­
lines and standards applying to awards to civilian employees.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11446 of January 16, 1969 (34 FR 803), Authorizing the Acceptance of Service Medals and Ribbons from Multilateral Organizations Other Than the United Nations, is a single paragraph. The President authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of Transportation (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations, and requires that a determination that service for such an organization is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619, 10629), section 62, amends the order by striking the words the Secretary of Transportation and inserting the words the Secretary of Homeland Security; section 92 of that order states that it becomes effective on March 1, 2003, so the amendment took effect on March 1, 2003. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor, but its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11446, and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so I do not treat EO 12977 as a later event. The OFR executive-order catalog lists only the amendment by EO 13286. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 13286 section 62, as a note to 5 U.S.C. 7342 with no ending statement. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation, supersession or other amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
